construction_markdown: No leaderboard construction is claimed. The proved result is an obstruction theorem for the standard asymptotic GS–Hadamard certificate. As a scope witness, the deterministic code \(\{(c,c):c\in\operatorname{RM}(1,29)\}\) has parameters \([2^{30},30,2^{29}]_2\) and shows that \(R_{\mathrm{template}}(m)\) is not a pointwise finite-length upper bound, even at a GS rational-function-field level.
distance_audit: Every nonzero word of \(\operatorname{RM}(1,m-1)\) has weight at least \(2^{m-2}\): nonconstant affine functions are balanced, while the nonzero constant function has full weight.
If a nonzero outer word has at least \(D\) nonzero symbols, injectivity of the inner map gives at least \(D\) disjoint nonzero inner blocks, hence binary weight at least \(D d_{\mathrm{in}}\).
Zero padding preserves dimension and absolute minimum distance but decreases relative distance; the occupied-length fraction \(\lambda\) is included in the proof.
For \(m=8\), the exact required outer distance is \(469,762,048/64=7,340,032\).
The finite \(m=30\) witness has distance \(2\cdot2^{28}=2^{29}>469,762,048\), but dimension only 30.
Designed outer distance and product distance are lower bounds. Stronger actual-distance or symbol-distribution arguments are outside the ceiling theorem.
explicitness_audit: The ceiling proof and all finite arithmetic are deterministic and symbolic; no random existence or sampled codewords are used.
The \(m=30\) scope witness is specified directly as a doubled Reed–Muller code and requires no unspecified field representation.
No special divisor, actual-distance bonus, or additional evaluation place is assumed to exist.
No repository files were modified; this is an obstruction result rather than a leaderboard submission.
The BPRS finite-genus bound is applied with \(q=16=2^4\), \(p=2\), \(r=4\), \(k=4\), and \(s=3\), satisfying its stated hypotheses.

obstructions: The displayed \(R_{\mathrm{template}}(m)\) is an asymptotic certificate envelope, not a finite or universal code-theoretic upper bound.
There is no globally weakest hypothesis under logical implication: outer-rate, actual-distance, concatenated-distance, inner-code, and alphabet-reduction improvements are independent.
Holding the \(m=8\) inner code and product analysis fixed, crossing requires an outer \(\mathbb F_{256}\) point strictly above \((R,\Delta)=(7/120,7/8)\). No such outer code is proved here.
The verified finite certificate is 28,280 outer dimensions below the first \(m=8\) ceiling crossing.
At the current \((4,3)\) level, improving only the genus estimate cannot suffice: BPRS forces a residual deficit of at least 11,000 outer dimensions.
At fixed inner length 128, averaging forces every binary \([128,8,d]\) code to have \(d\le64\); the RM inner code is already optimal for that length.

proof_markdown:
### The restricted certificate

Let \(m\in2\mathbb Z_{>0}\) and put
\[
h=2^{m-1},\qquad d_0=2^{m-2}=h/2,\qquad q=2^{m/2},\qquad \gamma_m=\frac1{q-1}.
\]
The code \(\operatorname{RM}(1,m-1)\) consists of affine functions on \(\mathbb F_2^{m-1}\). It has parameters \([h,m,d_0]_2\): every nonconstant affine function is balanced, and the nonzero constant function has weight \(h\).

Consider outer AG evaluation codes of length \(L_j\), genus \(g_j\), and divisor degree \(a_j<L_j\). Concatenate symbolwise with this RM code and append zeros to a binary length \(n_j\ge hL_j\). Define
\[
\lambda_j=\frac{hL_j}{n_j}\le1.
\]
The vanilla certificate credits only
\[
K_j^{\rm RR}=[a_j+1-g_j]_+,
\qquad D_j^{\rm des}=L_j-a_j,
\]
and uses the product distance \(d_0D_j^{\rm des}\).

The target distance implies
\[
\frac h2(L_j-a_j)\ge\frac7{16}n_j,
\]
so
\[
\frac{a_j}{L_j}\le1-\frac7{8\lambda_j}.
\tag{1}
\]
Consequently the credited binary rate is bounded by
\[
\begin{aligned}
R_j^{\rm cert}
&=\frac{m[a_j+1-g_j]_+}{n_j}\\
&\le\frac mh\left[
\lambda_j\left(1-\frac{g_j-1}{L_j}\right)-\frac78
\right]_+.
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}
\]
For a GS sequence, \((g_j-1)/L_j\to\gamma_m\). Since \(\lambda_j\le1\), (2) yields
\[
\limsup_jR_j^{\rm cert}
\le
\frac m{2^{m-1}}
\left(\frac18-\frac1{2^{m/2}-1}\right)_+.
\tag{3}
\]
Conversely, taking an asymptotically full GS evaluation set, no padding, and \(a_j=\lfloor L_j/8\rfloor\) approaches the right side whenever it is positive. Thus (3) is the exact envelope of this restricted asymptotic accounting.

### Optimization over every even extension degree

Write \(m=2s\). The parenthesis in (3) is positive precisely when \(2^s-1>8\), hence precisely when \(s\ge4\). Therefore the expression is zero for \(m=2,4,6\). At \(m=8\),
\[
R_{\rm template}(8)
=\frac8{128}\left(\frac18-\frac1{15}\right)
=\frac1{16}\frac7{120}
=\frac7{1920}.
\]
For even \(m\ge10\),
\[
R_{\rm template}(m)<\frac m{2^{m+2}}.
\]
The comparison sequence decreases along even integers because
\[
\frac{(m+2)/2^{m+4}}{m/2^{m+2}}= rac{m+2}{4m}<1.
\]
Thus
\[
R_{\rm template}(m)<\frac{10}{2^{12}}= rac5{2048}<\frac7{1920}.
\]
This proves that \(m=8\) is the unique maximizer.

### Why this is not a finite upper bound

Riemann–Roch actually gives
\[
\ell(G)=\deg G+1-g+i(G),\qquad i(G)=\ell(K-G)\ge0.
\tag{4}
\]
Thus bare RR is a lower dimension guarantee, not an upper bound on the evaluation code. Similarly, \(L-\deg G\) and the concatenation product are only lower bounds on actual distance. Finally, the GS ratio is asymptotic and supplies no pointwise inequality \((g-1)/L\ge1/(q-1)\).

There is even a finite pointwise counterexample inside the ordinary framework. At \(m=30\), take two rational evaluation places on the rational first tower level and \(G=0\). The outer code is \([2,1,2]_{2^{30}}\). Concatenating with \(\operatorname{RM}(1,29)=[2^{29},30,2^{28}]_2\) gives
\[
[2^{30},30,2^{29}]_2.
\]
But
\[
2^{30}R_{\rm template}(30)
=60\left(\frac18-\frac1{32767}\right)<\frac{15}{2}<30.
\]
Hence the displayed function is not a finite per-\(m\) upper bound. The witness remains far below the global \(7/1920\) score.

### Sharp holding-all-else-fixed escape

Keep \(m=8\), the \([128,8,64]\) inner code, ordinary unpadded concatenation, and product-distance analysis. If an outer family has rate \(\rho\) and relative distance \(\Delta\), then
\[
R_{\rm bin}=\frac\rho{16},
\qquad
\delta_{\rm bin}\ge\frac\Delta2.
\]
Therefore this interface crosses the envelope exactly when
\[
\Delta\ge\frac78,
\qquad
\rho>\frac7{120}.
\tag{5}
\]
There is no globally weakest hypothesis because improvements to the outer rate, actual distance, concatenated-distance analysis, or inner code are incomparable. Once all other ingredients are fixed, however, (5) is the sharp scalar relaxation.

A particularly local algebraic realization would replace bare RR by an exact special-divisor computation. If \(a_j/L_j\to1/8\), \(g_j/L_j\to1/15\), and \(i(G_j)/L_j\to\sigma\), then
\[
R_{\rm bin}\to\frac7{1920}+\frac\sigma{16}.
\]
Thus \(i(G_j)=o(L_j)\) cannot cross the envelope, whereas any proved \(\sigma>0\) permits it. Clifford's theorem bounds
\[
\sigma\le\frac1{15}-\frac1{16}= rac1{240},
\]
so this route, if realized, lies between \(7/1920\) and \(1/256\). For even \(m\ge10\), the optimal divisor degree is eventually above \(2g-2\), since \(1/8>2/(2^{m/2}-1)\); it is then nonspecial. This singles out \(m=8\) as the only maximizing degree where speciality can affect the standard asymptotic divisor.

For comparison, replacing only the inner code by \([\ell,8,d]_2\) while retaining the outer TVZ line gives
\[
\Phi_8(\ell,d)=\frac8\ell\left(\frac{14}{15}-\frac{7\ell}{16d}\right)_+.
\]
Direct algebra shows
\[
\Phi_8(\ell,d)>\frac7{1920}
\iff
(2048-\ell)d>960\ell.
\tag{6}
\]
At \(\ell=128\), (6) requires \(d\ge65\). Across all 255 nonzero words of a binary eight-dimensional code, each nonzero generator-matrix column contributes 128 ones, so \(255d\le128\ell\). Hence \(d\le64\) when \(\ell=128\). Likewise, retaining \(d=64\) forces \(\ell\ge128\). An inner-only escape must therefore alter the joint length-distance tradeoff, not just improve one parameter of RM.

### Exact finite \(m=8\) interface

Since
\[
\frac7{1920}2^{30}=3,914,683+\frac{11}{15},
\]
a general binary code first crosses at dimension \(3,914,684\). An \(m=8\) concatenated dimension is divisible by eight, so it needs
\[
k\ge3,914,688,
\qquad K_{\rm out}\ge489,336.
\tag{7}
\]
Let
\[
T=\frac{2^{30}}{128}=8,388,608.
\]
An exact finite outer escape is therefore any deterministic \(\mathbb F_{256}\)-linear code satisfying
\[
L\le T,
\qquad D\ge7,340,032,
\qquad K\ge489,336.
\tag{8}
\]
Concatenation and zero padding would then give exact length \(2^{30}\), distance at least the target, and dimension at least \(3,914,688\).

For designed distance, write \(L=T-p\) and choose \(a=L-7,340,032\). With genus bound \(\bar g\) and an additional certified dimension surplus \(s\),
\[
K_{\rm cert}= rac T8-(p+\bar g-1)+s.
\]
Condition (7) is equivalent to
\[
p+\bar g-1-s\le559,240.
\tag{9}
\]
The verified baseline has \(p=32,768\), \(\bar g=554,753\), and \(s=0\), giving aggregate loss \(587,520\). It is therefore short by exactly \(28,280\) outer dimensions.

Finally, the densified-tower lower genus bound gives
\[
g_{4,3}\ge(g_4-1)2^3+1,
\qquad g_4=67,185,
\]
so \(g_{4,3}\ge537,473\). Even with this smallest possible genus, bare RR at the fixed \(L\) gives at most
\[
1,015,808+1-537,473=478,336,
\]
which is 11,000 below (7). Hence exact-genus sharpening alone cannot cross at the current level. No required speciality, distance gain, or extra-place theorem is presently available, so no leaderboard construction follows.

research_direction: The all-even-degree numerical maximum is rigorously certified, but its scope is narrowed to the asymptotic bare-RR/designed-distance/product-distance proof calculus. Holding the maximizing m=8 interface fixed, the least structural escape is a strict outer improvement above rate 7/120 at relative distance 7/8—most locally via exact special-divisor or actual-distance information.
theorem_statement: For every positive even m, the asymptotic one-level Garcia–Stichtenoth plus RM(1,m−1) certificate that credits only bare Riemann–Roch dimension, designed outer distance, product concatenation distance, and zero padding has rate envelope \(R_{\mathrm{template}}(m)=\frac{m}{2^{m-1}}(\frac18-\frac1{2^{m/2}-1})_+\). Its unique maximum is \(7/1920\) at \(m=8\). This is not a pointwise finite or universal upper bound on actual GS-derived codes. With \(m=8\), RM(1,7), and ordinary product analysis fixed, an asymptotic crossing is equivalent to an outer \(\mathbb F_{256}\) code with relative distance at least \(7/8\) and rate strictly greater than \(7/120\); at block length \(2^{30}\), it requires \(L\le8,388,608\), \(D\ge7,340,032\), and \(K\ge489,336\). At the current level, exact-genus sharpening alone remains at least 11,000 outer dimensions short.
